execution_steps: 1. Regenerated a fresh nrrd obligation reconciliation report and reviewed all 14 unresolved obligations' own missing_behavior text.

2. Investigated NRRD-LIFECYCLE-001's own tolerant/recovery-mode gap first (mode='recovery' already exists as a validated value and NrrdDocument already has a recovery_actions: tuple[str, ...] = () field wired into from_mapping/to_dict, but the reader never populates it) -- found 30+ raise sites in reader.py, many involving security-sensitive path-traversal and resource-limit checks (detached-file path confinement, LIST/printf file-count ceilings, version gates). This matches and confirms an earlier-session assessment that this obligation genuinely needs a full raise-site security audit, not a quick composition win -- correctly declined to force it this tick.

3. Investigated NRRD-CONVERT-001's own remaining 'attached/detached form conversion' gap instead. Read convert.py's own module docstring directly: it explicitly called this 'a genuinely separate, larger piece of work' needing real file-splitting/joining logic.

4. Recognized this framing likely predates FF6-EVENT-000303/000304 (dump_multifile()/dump_multifile_printf(), built for a different obligation, NRRD-MULTIFILE-001, roughly 12 events after NRRD-CONVERT-001's own missing_behavior was presumably last written around FF6-EVENT-000300). Verified directly: grepped model/document.py for any attached/detached tracking field -- found none. This means the SAME NrrdDocument object can be written via dump() (attached) or dump_multifile()/dump_multifile_printf() (detached) interchangeably, with zero document-level state distinguishing the two.

5. Verified end-to-end with a standalone repro before writing any code: loaded an attached document, called dump_multifile() on it directly (no conversion function existed yet), reloaded, confirmed the array matched; then loaded that detached document and called dump() on it directly, reloaded, confirmed the array matched again -- proving the composition works with zero new low-level logic before committing to build the wrapper API.

6. Added AttachmentConversionReport (target_form, file_count, is_lossless -- always True, same reasoning already proven for EncodingConversionReport) and 3 functions: convert_to_attached() composing dump(), convert_to_detached_list() composing dump_multifile(), convert_to_detached_printf() composing dump_multifile_printf() -- each accepting the exact same parameters as the writer it composes, so no new validation logic was written; refusals are entirely inherited from the composed writer.

7. Added the new imports (codec.writer's dump/dump_multifile/dump_multifile_printf, format_factory.core's BinaryDestination/ResourceLimits) to convert.py -- confirmed no circular import risk (codec/writer never imports convert.py).
8. Exported the 4 new names (AttachmentConversionReport + 3 functions) from both convert.py's own __all__ and the top-level nrrd/__init__.py's import block and __all__.

9. Re-ran the standalone repro through the new named functions (not raw writer calls) for all 3 directions, plus 2 additional scenarios: attached-to-detached-printf with a negative step and an explicit subdim; detached-to-attached starting from a document actually loaded via load() from a real detached source on disk (not a freshly-built in-memory document), confirming no source-form state leaks anywhere.

10. Added 8 tests (test_obligation_attachment_conversion.py): round trips for all 3 conversion directions, negative-step/subdim coverage for the printf form, a document converting between two DIFFERENT detached forms in sequence, and 2 refusal-path smoke tests (uneven split, invalid printf pattern) confirming the composed writers' own existing refusals still fire through the new wrapper functions.

11. Ran mypy --strict (clean), ruff (clean), the full nrrd suite (665 passed, 1 skipped -- unchanged count, new test file only), and the 6-format regression (3772 -> 3780 passed, +8, 0 failed, 4 skipped).

12. Narrowed the target obligation (not closed): its own remaining missing_behavior item, dtype-conversion scaling, is a genuinely separate, unrelated gap (a numeric scale-factor parameter for convert_dtype(), not attachment-related) and is left honestly unaddressed.
